recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed unless the Vocabulary work group later chooses to change the semantics of hierarchical ValueSet expansions rather than retain the existing navigational-only rule.
issue_request: FHIR-8042 was a Published FHIR-core ValueSet issue with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It asked to remove recursive containment from ValueSet.expansion, but the approved Vocabulary work group decision kept hierarchical expansions and required clarification that nested contains elements do not imply logical relationships, cannot be used for logical inferencing, and exist to help human users navigate expansion codes.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git/SVN commit 9bc3b77afaeb0acd3f6333788b85dd0a5a350463, '#8042 - clarify use of heirarchical expansions', matching the Jira comment 'svn revision 5734'. That commit added the approved wording to source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml. Later source rework carried the rule forward, and the current StructureDefinition source includes the matching comment on ValueSet.expansion.contains.contains.
additional_context: ValueSet is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml and source/valueset/structuredefinition-ValueSet.xml are current build-scope evidence. Jira concept searches found only FHIR-8042, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no related or conflicting later evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source edit was made because the current source already preserves both parts of the approved decision: the narrative Hierarchical Expansions note and the recursive contains element comment.
